questions.text: Count out loud: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, ___. What number comes next?
questions.explanation: When counting by ones, the number that comes right after 9 is 10.

questions.text: Count the stars: ★ ★ ★ ★ ★ ★ ★. How many stars are there?
questions.explanation: Touch and count each star one at a time. There are 7 stars in all.

questions.text: Which shape has 3 sides and 3 corners?
questions.explanation: A triangle has exactly 3 sides and 3 corners. A circle has none, and a square and a rectangle each have 4.

questions.text: A ball is sitting on top of a box. Where is the ball?
questions.explanation: When something sits on top of another object, it is above it.
Adding 1 more to 4 gives the next counting number, which is 5.

questions.text: Start counting from 6. Which shows the next three numbers?
questions.explanation: Counting on from 6, the next three numbers are 7, 8, 9. You do not say 6 again, and you do not skip 7.

questions.text: There are 3 birds on a branch. 2 more birds fly over and land. How many birds are on the branch now?
questions.explanation: More birds landing means adding. 3 + 2 = 5 birds on the branch.

questions.text: There are 4 frogs on a log. 2 frogs jump off. Which number sentence shows this story?
questions.explanation: Frogs jumping off means taking away, which is subtraction. Start with 4 and take away 2: 4 - 2.

questions.text: Group A has 3 dots. Group B has 5 dots. Which is true?
questions.explanation: 5 is greater than 3, so Group B has more dots than Group A.

questions.text: You have a pencil and a crayon. Which word names a way to measure and compare them?
questions.explanation: Length is something you can measure. You can compare the pencil and crayon by how long each one is. Color, flavor, and sound are not lengths you can measure.

questions.text: You have 3 red apples, 2 green apples, and 4 bananas. How many pieces of fruit are apples?
questions.explanation: Count only the apples: 3 red and 2 green. 3 + 2 = 5 apples. The 4 bananas are not apples, so they are not counted.

questions.text: The number 14 is made of one group of ten and some ones. How many ones are left over?
questions.explanation: 14 is 1 ten and 4 ones. After the group of ten, there are 4 ones left over.

questions.text: You have 7. How many more do you need to make 10?
questions.explanation: Count up from 7 to 10: 8, 9, 10. That is 3 more, so 7 + 3 = 10.

questions.text: Which two groups can you put together to make 5?
questions.explanation: 2 and 3 make 5 because 2 + 3 = 5. The others make 4, 4, and 6.

questions.text: A circle and a square are both flat shapes. How are they different?
options: The square has straight sides and the circle does not
The circle has straight sides and the square does not
questions.explanation: A square has 4 straight sides and 4 corners. A circle is round with no straight sides and no corners, so the square has straight sides and the circle does not.
